Hi. Is this the Administration class?
It is. I am Rafa. What is your major?
Administration too. I am in my third semester.
Same. Do you work?
Not yet. I am looking for an internship for next semester.
Me too. I apply for two or three every week. Nobody answers.
They all want English. My English is fine on paper, but I stop and think too much when I speak.
You are speaking right now and you are not stopping.
That is different. You are not a job interview.
Fair. See you Thursday, then.
I study Business Administration in Sao Paulo.
I am in my third semester.
I am looking for an internship.
Give me one second, I am thinking.
How do you say this in English?

Okay, so I got it. The internship. I still cannot believe it. Listen, I applied to eleven places. Eleven. And nine of them never answered, which is normal, apparently. The interview was twenty minutes and only three questions were in English: what I study, why I want to work there, and what I do on weekends. That is it. Nothing complicated. So here is my advice, and I am serious about this: prepare four sentences about yourself and say them out loud before the call. Not in your head. Out loud. Because in your head everything sounds perfect.

Good morning. A quick note about the careers fair. It is on Thursday, from ten in the morning until five in the afternoon, in Building B. Twenty-two companies are coming this year, and eight of them are looking for students in their third or fourth semester, so that is most of you. Bring your student card. If you have a CV in English, bring it too, and bring several copies. And one last thing: talk to the small companies. Everybody stands in the queue for the big names and nobody talks to the small ones. Thank you.
